details.description: Polyglot is one of the voice types offered by Google Cloud Text-to-Speech, listed alongside Standard, WaveNet, Neural2, Studio, and Chirp 3: HD voices in Google's own voice-type documentation. As of Google's current voice list it comprises six voices — en-AU-Polyglot-1, en-US-Polyglot-1, fr-FR-Polyglot-1, de-DE-Polyglot-1, es-ES-Polyglot-1, and es-US-Polyglot-1, all male — making it Google's smallest TTS voice type by language and voice coverage. Google's documentation does not mark Polyglot as deprecated or legacy, but also does not publish a dedicated description of its underlying technology or intended use case.
advantages: Remains listed as an active, non-deprecated voice type in Google's current Text-to-Speech voice-type documentation.
Available in six locales — Australian English, US English, French, German, and Spanish (Spain and US) — each with a dedicated Polyglot-1 voice, per Google's voice list.
disadvantages: Limited to six voices (en-AU-Polyglot-1, en-US-Polyglot-1, fr-FR-Polyglot-1, de-DE-Polyglot-1, es-ES-Polyglot-1, es-US-Polyglot-1), all male, far fewer than Google's Standard, WaveNet, or Neural2 tiers.
Google's documentation does not publish a dedicated description of Polyglot's underlying technology or recommended use case, unlike its Neural2, Studio, and Chirp 3: HD voice types.
use_cases: General-purpose text-to-speech output in Australian English, US English, French, German, or Spanish (Spain or US) where a male Polyglot voice is wanted.
Applications already using Google Cloud Text-to-Speech that want an additional male voice option in one of these six locales.

sources.title: Supported voices and languages | Cloud Text-to-Speech

notes: Google's docs give minimal detail on Polyglot beyond its voice list (no dedicated feature description, unlike Neural2/Studio/Chirp), so the write-up is thinner than usual but every claim traces to the voice-type or supported-voices pages. Corrected the voice count against Google's current supported-voices table (last updated 2026-09-18): Polyglot has six voices, not three — en-AU, en-US, fr-FR, de-DE, es-ES, and es-US, all male; the original write-up missed the German and two Spanish voices. Catalog facts give no conflicting token or deprecation values.
